tasks.title: Most frequent words
tasks.statement: Write a function top_words(text, n): a list of the n most frequent words of the text (words are separated by spaces, ignore case) as tuples (word, count) in descending order of frequency. Use Counter.

tasks.title: Anagrams
tasks.statement: Write a function is_anagram(a, b): True if the words consist of the same letters (case and spaces do not matter). Compare the letter counters.
tasks.hint: Lowercase both, remove the spaces and compare Counter(a) == Counter(b).

tasks.title: Groups by length
tasks.statement: Write a function group_by_length(words): a dictionary "length → list of words of that length" in the original order. Use defaultdict(list) and return an ordinary dict.
tasks.hint: groups[len(w)].append(w); at the end return dict(groups).

tasks.title: Moving average
tasks.statement: Write a function moving_average(nums, k): the average of each window of k consecutive numbers (full windows only). Use a deque with maxlen=k.
tasks.hint: window = deque(maxlen=k); for each x: append; if len(window) == k, add sum(window) / k.

tasks.title: Breadth-first traversal
tasks.statement: Write a function bfs_order(graph, start): the order of vertices in a breadth-first traversal of the graph. graph is a dictionary "vertex → list of neighbors". Use a deque; visit each vertex once.
tasks.hint: queue = deque([start]); seen is a dictionary of visited vertices; popleft, then add the neighbors not seen yet.

tasks.title: A point as a namedtuple
tasks.statement: Create a named tuple Point with fields x and y, and a function distance(p, q), the Euclidean distance between two points (use math.hypot).
tasks.hint: Point = namedtuple("Point", ["x", "y"]); distance: math.hypot(p.x - q.x, p.y - q.y).

tasks.title: k largest
tasks.statement: Write a function k_largest(nums, k): the k largest numbers in descending order. Use the heapq module.
tasks.hint: heapq.nlargest(k, nums) already returns them in descending order.

tasks.title: Grade from a score
tasks.statement: Write a function grade(score): 0–59 → "E", 60–69 → "D", 70–79 → "C", 80–89 → "B", 90–100 → "A". Use bisect and a list of boundaries, with no chain of ifs.

tasks.title: Merge sorted lists
tasks.statement: Write a function merge_sorted(lists): one sorted list built from several already sorted lists. Use heapq.merge.
